question: On palpating a large abdominal mass, you cannot get above it (your hand cannot slip superiorly between the mass and the costal margin), and the notch is palpable on the medial border. Which organ is this most likely to be?

answers.text: Liver — you cannot get above a hepatomegaly and the notch is on the inferior border anteriorly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The liver does not have a notch on the medial border. The hepatic notch corresponds to the falciform ligament and is felt anteriorly on the inferior surface, not the medial border.

answers.text: Spleen — you cannot get above a splenomegaly and the splenic notch is palpable on the medial (superomedial) border

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The spleen is in the left hypochondrium under the ribs: you cannot get above it, it moves diagonally towards the right iliac fossa with respiration, and the characteristic notch on the superomedial border clinches the diagnosis.

answers.text: Kidney — you cannot get above a large kidney and it has a notch on its medial border (hilum)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A kidney is retroperitoneal: it is bimanually ballotable and you CAN get above it (the hand slips between mass and costal margin). The splenic notch is the classic teaching sign.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: splenomegaly = cannot get above it + moves diagonally + notch on superomedial border. Kidney is ballotable and you can get above it; liver notch is anterior-inferior, not medial.
Correct. Cannot-get-above + diagonal movement + medial notch = spleen. These three signs together are pathognomonic of splenomegaly.
